sources.entry: Claude Squad by smtg-ai - A terminal app that manages multiple Claude Code, Codex, and other local agents (including Aider) in separate workspaces, allowing you to work on multiple tasks simultaneously.

summary.one_liner: Claude Squad is a terminal app (installed as `cs`) that runs multiple coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and Aider, each in its own isolated git workspace.
summary.what_it_does: Claude Squad lets you start and manage several AI coding agent sessions from one terminal window. Each session runs in its own tmux session and its own git worktree on a separate branch, so parallel tasks do not conflict. You can create sessions with a prompt, attach to reprompt an agent, and pause or resume sessions. Its menu also covers reviewing diffs in a preview/diff tab, committing and pushing a session's branch to GitHub, and checking out changes. An experimental autoyes flag auto-accepts prompts for Claude Code and Aider. Profiles in a JSON config let you define several named launch commands and pick one when creating a session.
use_cases: run several coding agents on different tasks at once
review AI-generated changes before pushing them
isolate parallel agent work on separate git branches
run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or Aider from one terminal
background agent tasks in auto-accept mode
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash  (manual install; puts cs in ~/.local/bin)
stack: Go (inferred from the binary and install tooling; not stated in README)
notable: Each task gets its own git worktree and branch, so parallel agents do not conflict
Supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and Aider, plus other local agents via -p flag
Named profiles in config.json let you switch between launch commands per session
Review diffs and checkout changes before pushing to GitHub
caveats: Requires tmux and the GitHub CLI (gh) to be installed
README notes that a timeout waiting for tmux may require updating the underlying program to its latest version
